marks.gloss_en: והלא דברים קל וחומר: ומה זה שלא ציער עצמו אלא מן היין נקרא חוטא, המצער עצמו מכל דבר ודבר על אחת כמה וכמה
R' Elazar HaKappar's conclusion: one who distresses himself from each and every thing -- all the more so [is called a sinner]
ומה זה שלא ציער עצמו אלא מדבר אחד נקרא קדוש, המצער עצמו מכל דבר על אחת כמה וכמה
R' Elazar: as it is said 'he shall be holy, letting the locks of his hair grow' (Num 6:5)
מרעב מיבעי ליה! אלא הכי קאמר: בשכר שמרעיב עצמו -- the verse's 'in famine' is read as reward for famine-starving
Rav (via Rav Yehuda): whoever starves himself in years of famine is saved from an unusual death
שכן מצינו במשה רבינו שציער עצמו עם הצבור -- Moses' precedent
rather, a person should be distressed together with the community
סבר כי האי תנא, דתניא: רבי אלעזר הקפר ברבי -- Shmuel holds like R' Elazar HaKappar's kal vachomer
Shmuel: whoever sits in a fast is called a sinner
ולשמואל, הא איקרי קדוש! -- the nazirite is called holy (Num 6:5)
ההוא אגידול פרע קאי -- that refers to the growth of the locks
ולרבי אלעזר, הא נקרא חוטא! -- the nazirite is called a sinner (Num 6:11)
ההוא דסאיב נפשיה -- that is one who made himself impure [by a corpse]
ומי אמר רבי אלעזר הכי? והאמר רבי אלעזר: לעולם ימוד אדם עצמו כאילו קדוש שרוי בתוך מעיו -- he forbids burdening the body
[the stam: what is between them?] the difference is one who sits in a boat
Rav Pappa would eat one loaf at each and every parasang
Reish Lakish: a person is forbidden to have marital relations in years of famine

when Israel is in distress and one separates from them, the two ministering angels who accompany a man place their hands on his head and say: this one who separated from the community -- let him not see the community's consolation
when the community is in distress, let no one say: I will go home and eat and drink, and peace upon you, my soul
up to here is the measure of the middling

and lest a person say 'who testifies against me?' -- the stones and beams of his house testify against him, as it is said 'for the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it' (Hab 2:11)
R' Chidka: a person's soul testifies against him, as it is said 'from her that lies in your bosom guard the doors of your mouth' (Mic 7:5)
'a God of faithfulness' (Deut 32:4): just as punishment is exacted from the wicked in the world to come even for a light sin, so it is exacted from the righteous in this world for a light sin
'and without iniquity': just as reward is paid to the righteous in the world to come even for a light mitzva, so it is paid to the wicked in this world even for a light mitzva

'just and right is He' -- they said: at a person's departure to his eternal home all his deeds are enumerated before him... they say 'sign!' and he signs, as it is said 'He seals the hand of every man' (Job 37:7)
